gen-press-start-2p-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Arcade-cabinet nostalgia, with letters pinned far apart on the line. The standout is the gap between Press Start 2P, with barely varying strokes, and Noto Sans Osmanya, a sans with wide, easy s turns.
gen-tourney-gf-hind-vadodara: Wide-tracked, athletic letters hit hard up top. Tourney keeps every stroke one width while Hind Vadodara, a sans with open, tall-bowled a and e, gives the eye somewhere to rest.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam keeps its curve endings well apart. Tourney excels at blunt, bulky impact with no swelling in its bowls, whereas the body does tall, full c, s and z shapes.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hiero: Blunt, marker-tipped lettering with real swagger. Tourney does best at chunky, round-tipped impact, while Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs does best at modern, outward-pointing terminals and an x-height nearly touching cap height.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-readex-pro: Bold, expressive lettering with short ascenders and a tall x-height makes Grandstander hard to miss. And Readex Pro, a sans with broad terminal gaps and steady weight, should read smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-quicksand: Tight, sturdy headings meet soft round bulbs. Oswald is best at packing text into confident, tightly knit rows, while Quicksand is best at uninterrupted monoline strokes and tall, bulb-round lowercase.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-akatab: Dense, confident heading rows that hit hard from the first glance. Akatab, with round letters that look cupped rather than clenched, would soften things if Oswald were made small.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-nko: Tight, confident rows of heading text with plenty of punch. Noto Sans NKo, a sans with see-through c openings, should keep paragraphs of text moving smoothly line after line beside Oswald.
